get_emas_order_spot_first.meaning: OraclePack.getEMAs() returns its tuple in the order (spotEMA, fastEMA, slowEMA, eonsEMA, medianTick), i.e. spotEMA is the first returned value
get_emas_order_spot_first.checkpoint: before twapEMA() destructures the getEMAs() return tuple

twap_ema_value.meaning: TWAP value returned by RiskEngine.twapEMA() and consumed by the StaleOracle safety boundary and solvency evaluation
twap_ema_value.checkpoint: after twapEMA() computes the blend from the getEMAs() tuple

stale_oracle_outcome_occurs.meaning: the altered TWAP changes the outcome of the StaleOracle safety boundary / solvency evaluation, so the system proceeds when it should revert as stale or reverts when it should proceed
stale_oracle_outcome_occurs.checkpoint: at StaleOracle safety boundary / solvency evaluation using the returned TWAP

assumptions: The getEMAs() return order (spotEMA, fastEMA, slowEMA, eonsEMA, medianTick) is fixed before twapEMA() destructures it.
The StaleOracle safety boundary and solvency evaluation consume the TWAP value returned by twapEMA().

unresolved.description: The report states the altered TWAP changes StaleOracle/solvency outcomes (proceed-when-should-revert or revert-when-should-proceed) but gives no numeric TWAP threshold, tick value, or stale-boundary comparison, so the outcome-change relation is carried as a grounded Boolean rather than a numeric inequality.

limitations: The report does not establish a concrete prior price-movement transaction or numeric tick values; spotEMA propagation is conditional and not formalized here.
Blocked liquidations and incorrect liquidations are stated as possible (may), not observed incidents, and are handled in separate claim-generation passes.
No attacker actor or permissionless-call condition is stated; this is a latent implementation defect, not an observed exploit.
